name: Hadadezer
bio: Hadadezer son of Rehob was the king of Zobah, a powerful Aramean kingdom, whom David struck down while Hadadezer was on his way to restore his control along the Euphrates. David captured a thousand of his chariots, seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers, hamstringing the chariot horses except for a hundred he kept back, and went on to defeat the Arameans of Damascus who came to Hadadezer's aid (2 Samuel 8:3-6). David took the gold shields carried by Hadadezer's officers and dedicated them, along with bronze plundered from his cities, to the LORD (2 Samuel 8:7-8, 11-12); word of Hadadezer's defeat also prompted King Toi of Hamath, his old rival, to send his own son Joram to David with gifts and congratulations (2 Samuel 8:9-10).
